newsitem.title: INDIA: India hopes talks with Pakistan will resume soon.
newsitem.headline: India hopes talks with Pakistan will resume soon.

text.p: Indian Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral is expected to write to his Pakistani counterpart proposing the two countries resume stalled peace talks on a wide range of issues, a government official said on Saturday.
"He is writing the letter today," a foreign ministry official told Reuters.

Gujral told the Press Trust of India news agency earlier on Saturday there had been a big improvement in India's relationship with neighbours Bangladesh and Nepal, and that things were moving in the right direction with Pakistan.

Pakistan's new Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said in a recent letter to Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda that foreign ministry secretaries of the two countries meet before the end of March to "prepare the ground for meaningful discussions" between the two prime ministers.

The letter responded to one sent by Deve Gowda on February 17 to congratulate Sharif on taking office and proposing a resumption of talks on a wide range of issues, including the disputed Himalayan region of Jammu and Kashmir.
The two countries have fought three wars since independence from Britain in 1947, two of them over Kashmir, two-thirds of which is ruled by India and the rest by Pakistan.
